slides.main: Not absorbing large amounts of fructose is normal, even when healthy.
slides.sub: When it turns into an intolerance, and what to try instead of giving up fruit.

slides.main: In a small study, most healthy adults absorbed 25 g fructose, not 50 g.
slides.sub: Below 25 g, healthy volunteers had no tummy symptoms, even those with proven malabsorption.

slides.main: Fructose in excess of glucose is thought to be absorbed worst.
slides.sub: Apples, pears, mangoes, honey and high fructose corn syrup are high. Sorbitol in sugar-free sweets is poorly absorbed too.

slides.main: A breath test reading on its own is not an intolerance.
slides.sub: Your symptoms are recorded during the test, and results can vary when the test is repeated.

slides.main: A common approach: cut down briefly, then reintroduce foods.
slides.sub: One at a time, to find how much you tolerate. Don't cut foods out without advice from a GP or dietitian.

slides.main: Get medical help if you have:
items: Vomiting or low blood sugar after sweets
Blood in your stool or black stools
Symptoms that wake you up at night
